task.title: Modulo operation
task.prompt: Support % in calculate() and the console menu using Python's modulo semantics. Reject modulo by zero with ValueError and keep the console running. Preserve +, -, *, /, finite-number input validation, and clean quit behavior.
task.description: Extend the console calculator with a modulo (remainder) operation.

data.summary: Added support for the modulo (%) operation in the calculator, including input validation and error handling for modulo by zero. The console menu and calculate() function now accept and process % as a valid operator, with appropriate error messages and continued operation on invalid input.

agents.system_prompt: You are the Programmer in a controlled coding study. Implement the supplied task and follow the plan if present. Preserve unrelated behavior. Return only JSON with "summary" (string) and "files" (object mapping changed relative paths to their complete replacement source text). data.summary: The change adds support for the modulo (%) operation to the calculator, updating both the calculation logic and the user interface prompts. It correctly handles modulo by zero by raising a ValueError, and updates all relevant error messages and operator checks. The implementation is consistent with the existing structure and preserves all previous behaviors.
limitations: No automated tests are provided to verify modulo behavior.
Modulo operation is only defined for numeric (float) inputs; Python's % operator on floats may have surprising results for some users.
No explicit handling for negative numbers or non-integer modulo, but this matches Python's semantics.
User input is still limited to finite numbers; no support for complex numbers or other numeric types.
